logline: A news anchor investigating a 1987 serial murder and a woman trying to prevent her parents' doomed marriage are thrown back in time together - and discover their missions are entangled.

renewal.note: Single-season run of 16 episodes; concluded June 20, 2023. No sequel announced.

bollymeter.basis: An 8.0 IMDb score and an enthusiastic reception from K-drama communities reflect a show whose emotional sincerity and consistent pacing outweigh its modest production values. The Fangirl Verdict graded it B++ for staying heartfelt from start to finish.

pull_quotes.text: A surprisingly engaging, heartfelt time travel mystery that stays nicely consistent, from start to finish.

seasons.review_body: My Perfect Stranger aired May 1 to June 20, 2023, on KBS2, averaging 4.4 percent nationwide - modest for linear broadcast but with a disproportionate online following that built through Kocowa, Viki, and Viu. The time-travel premise is used to serve two emotional tracks simultaneously: a murder mystery set in 1987 and a daughter's attempt to rewrite a painful family history. Kim Dong-wook and Jin Ki-joo earned wide praise for their chemistry. The Fangirl Verdict awarded a B++ and specifically called out the mother-daughter relationship as the show's emotional core - an element reviewers found more affecting than the procedural spine. Critics with reservations noted the time-travel logic occasionally strained and the serial killer plot was resolved with less rigor than it promised. The 8.0 IMDb score places it among the better-regarded KBS2 dramas of 2023.

episode_reviews.title: My Perfect Stranger
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The highest-rated episode in the series on IMDb at 8.9, the premiere executes the time-travel setup with clarity and establishes the two leads' mismatched objectives before dropping them both into 1987. The period atmosphere is sketched without nostalgia tourism, and the structural conceit - two strangers with secretly overlapping missions - generates immediate narrative energy.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment both characters realise their objectives in 1987 are not as separate as each assumed.

episode_reviews.title: The Reason You Can't Leave
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale ties together the serial killer resolution and the family history threads. The Fangirl Verdict's observation that the show manages to finish strong is borne out by audience engagement: the final episode accumulated IMDb ratings (8.1) above the series average, suggesting viewers who stayed were rewarded rather than disappointed.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Yoon Young's final conversation with Soon-ae - the moment the family thread finds its resolution and the show earns the emotional ground it has been laying since episode one.

critic_note.text: Show more than makes up for its shortcomings with how much heart it has, and manages to finish strong.
